name: FRITZ!Powerline 1240 AX WLAN Set
note: Kit is a 1240 AX (Wi-Fi 6 on 2.4 GHz only, 2 GbE) plus a 1210; real speed estimated at 25% of the PHY rate, no pass-through socket listed in the datasheet, watts from AVM idle 4.5 W and 2.4 W plus about 3 W under load.

name: FRITZ!Powerline 1220E Set
note: Real speed estimated at 25% of the PHY rate (PC-WELT measured under 250 Mbit/s with a 1220E/1260E pair in a flat); AVM states about 3 W average.

name: FRITZ!Powerline 1260E WLAN Set
note: Kit is a 1260E (1 GbE, dual-band Wi-Fi 5) plus a 1220E (2 GbE); real speed measured at just under 250 Mbit/s by PC-WELT (flat) and about 450 Mbit/s by basic-tutorials, watts averages 6.7 W and about 3 W.

name: FRITZ!Powerline 540E WLAN Set
note: Kit is a 540E (2 Fast Ethernet, Wi-Fi N300) plus a 510E; real speed estimated because Fast Ethernet caps TCP at about 90 Mbit/s, watts averages about 4 W and 2 W from AVM.

name: Magic 2 WiFi 6 next Starter Kit
note: Kit is one Wi-Fi 6 adapter (2 GbE, up to 3000 Mbit/s Wi-Fi) plus one LAN adapter; real speed about 350 Mbit/s as reported in one review on poor wiring, watts is the average of both adapters.

name: Magic 2 WiFi next Starter Kit
note: Kit is one Wi-Fi adapter (2 GbE, Wi-Fi 5 up to 1200 Mbit/s) plus one LAN adapter; real speed measured 228-427 Mbit/s LAN-to-WiFi next by ocinside; watts is the average of both adapters.

name: Magic 1 LAN 1-1 Starter Kit
note: Real speed estimated; devolo's datasheet caps the LAN-side rate at 330 Mbit/s because this is a single-stream (SISO) G.hn 1200 adapter.

name: Magic 2 LAN 1-1 Starter Kit
note: Real speed measured at 258-518 Mbit/s on a good circuit in the ocinside Magic 2 WiFi next test (same G.hn 2400 chipset), 450 chosen as typical; pairs only with other devolo Magic/G.hn units.

name: Magic 2 LAN triple Starter Kit
note: Kit is one triple adapter (3 GbE) plus one LAN adapter (1 GbE); real speed taken from Magic 2 measurements (258-518 Mbit/s, ocinside), power estimated from the Magic 2 LAN datasheet.

name: dLAN 550+ WiFi Starter Kit
note: Real speed estimated because the 100 Mbit/s Ethernet port caps TCP at about 90 Mbit/s (Wi-Fi N300 adapter plus a 550 duo+ partner); power estimated, price is the launch UVP.

name: dLAN 1200+ Starter Kit
note: Real speed measured by PC-WELT at 233-322 Mbit/s over short distance (2015); discontinued, price is an approximate street price.

name: Powerline 2000 + Extra Outlet (PLP2000)
note: Real speed estimated from Tom's Guide (101 Mbit/s through a 200 Mbit/s line, best of its tested kits) and owner reports of 90-230 Mbit/s; 3.7 W is Tom's Guide's measured load.

name: Powerline 1000 + Extra Outlet (PLP1000)
note: Real speed estimated at 20% of the PHY rate (Digitec measured only 49-72 Mbit/s on old wiring for the PL1000); datasheet lists HomePlug AV/Green PHY compatibility.

name: Powerline 2000 Connection Kit (myStrom PLC2000K)
note: Swisscom's page only recommends pairing myStrom adapters, so this is the myStrom Powerline 2000 Connection Kit (PLC2000K), whose own OEM is unknown; real speed from Swisscom's own tests of 150-300 Mbit/s.

name: TL-WPA8631P KIT (AV1300 Wi-Fi)
note: Kit is a WPA8631P Wi-Fi adapter (3 GbE, AC1200) plus a TL-PA8010P; real speed estimated from an owner report of about 350/300 Mbit/s, watts is the average of 11 W and 4.6 W typical.

name: TL-PA7017 KIT (AV1000)
note: Real speed estimated at 20% of the PHY rate (no independent measurement found); no pass-through socket (the TL-PA7017P kit has one).

name: TL-PA9020P KIT (AV2000)
note: Real speed estimated from mixed reports (Tom's Guide 43 Mbit/s through a 200 Mbit/s line, owners 120-380 Mbit/s); TP-Link only publishes max 5.8 W so typical power is estimated.

name: TL-PA8010P KIT (AV1300)
note: Real speed measured by APC Australia at about 220 Mbit/s (2017) and by Tech Advisor at about 100 Mbit/s (2015, AV1200 predecessor), 200 chosen as typical.

name: TL-PA4010 KIT (AV600)
note: Real speed estimated because the 10/100 Ethernet port caps TCP at about 90 Mbit/s; no pass-through socket (the TL-PA4010P kit has one).
